A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeepEyes research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, revised, and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original DeepEyes benchmark evaluations, training-dynamics analyses, reward and data ablations, and successful and failed reasoning cases.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds real-world benchmark evaluations, model/data scaling experiments, tool-generalization results, and a relevancy-map case study.

M1.justification: The core crop-based iMCoT procedure, GRPO training, and conditional reward remain unchanged. v3 Section 4.4 adds a crop-plus-rotate inference variant by exposing a rotation tool through the system prompt, explicitly without retraining or architectural changes.

E1.justification: v3 substantially extends evaluation coverage with MME-RealWorld-Lite and its separate perception/reasoning categories, plus HR-OCR-Rot, which introduces randomly rotated images from the HR-Bench-8K OCR subset. The original benchmarks and three-source base training corpus remain.

E2.justification: Pixel-Reasoner is added to the existing high-resolution comparison in Table 1 and participates in the new MME-RealWorld-Lite comparison. The earlier high-resolution comparator roster is otherwise retained.

E3.justification: New experiments compare 7B and 32B models trained on the same data, increase the reasoning-data fraction from 23% to 42%, and compare crop-only versus crop-plus-rotate inference on images rotated by 0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees. These substantially extend the experimental design; the original 7B training budget and stated hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds model-size and reasoning-data scaling analyses, a zero-shot tool-transfer test under image rotation, and a token-relevancy case study investigating hallucination mitigation. The original reward analysis, training dynamics, and six appendix cases remain. The data-composition ablation is relocated to Appendix B.2 rather than removed.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run evaluation statistics, seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates, and the retained training-dynamics plots do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original 7B benchmark scores remain unchanged, but substantial results are added: MME-RealWorld-Lite overall accuracy of 53.2; DeepEyes-32B scores of 93.3 on V* and 55.9 on WeMath; additional-reasoning-data scores of 51.8 on MathVerse and 43.6 on WeMath; and HR-OCR-Rot scores of 80.1 with cropping versus 83.6 with cropping plus rotation. These are new experimental conditions, not revisions of the original scores. The text-only CoT subcategory results from v1 Table 4 are omitted from v3's condensed Table 9.

T1.justification: The MDP state/action formulation and conditional reward equations remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs, and the new relevancy analysis introduces no substantive formal derivation.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain native interleaved visual/textual reasoning learned through end-to-end RL without cold-start SFT or external specialist models, supported by data selection and conditional rewards, with emergent reasoning patterns and training stages. The active-perception terminology and expanded experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations linking abstract reasoning to better perception and visual re-grounding to reduced language-driven hallucination. It softens the claim that joint optimization guarantees global optimality, but replaces v1's tentative distribution-shift explanation of HR-8K failures with stronger necessity and superiority claims. Some interpretations exceed the evidence: Section 4.4 claims superiority across all ablation benchmarks although Table 9 reports 75.1 versus 75.4 on HR-4K. The appendix's 7B-only and crop-only statements remain unupdated.

D1.justification: v3 documents the added reasoning-data proportion, rotation angles, and prompt-only tool integration, and describes setup instructions and training scripts at the existing code URL. Conversely, it omits v1's explicit eight responses per question for difficulty filtering. The original hardware, training hyperparameters, corpus counts, and appendix crop-tool prompts remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for Pixel-Reasoner, MME-RealWorld, the additional reasoning data, relevancy analysis, hallucination mechanisms, and two embodied/video works. These are limited extensions; the related-work taxonomy and positioning against predefined workflows and text-only reasoning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Extensive rewriting affects the abstract, introduction, method explanations, training-dynamics discussion, and results narrative, systematically emphasizing active perception instead of tool calling. The data-ablation discussion moves to Appendix B.2, the analysis section is reorganized, and author-contribution, LLM-usage, and reproducibility statements are added.

P2.justification: Four new experimental tables and a hallucination-relevancy figure substantially reorganize the empirical presentation. The iMCoT table is condensed, and the data-composition table moves to the appendix. The old reward-results display labeled Figure 5 becomes Table 5; v3 Figure 5 is genuinely new. Conference formatting, table sizing, and appendix figure placement also change, while the original case figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens evidence for scalability and transfer beyond v1's proposed 7B crop-only model through larger-model, data-scaling, and zero-shot rotation experiments, alongside broader real-world evaluation and a relevant new comparator. The net gain is limited by overstated interpretations: uniformly widening scaling advantages and superiority on every ablation benchmark contradict Tables 6 and 9. Reduced ablation detail and unchanged 7B-only/crop-only appendix statements also weaken completeness and consistency.
